Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
revision_notes: The cited CIPIT article is a regional survey of cross-border data-flow rules covering six countries (Kenya, Nigeria, Zambia and others); Eswatini is not among the country case studies discussed in the piece, so the citation does not specifically evidence the Eswatini score. Direct review of Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022, gazetted 4 March 2022), Part V (sections 32-33, Trans-Border Flow of Personal Information Outside Eswatini), confirms there is no requirement to store data within Eswatini's borders. The Act permits transfer of personal information to SADC member states under regional standards, and to non-SADC states where an adequacy assessment of the recipient jurisdiction's data protection safeguards is met (consistent with the Kenya-style consent/adequacy model, not the Nigeria/Zambia-style storage-mandate model). This supports Value Code 1 (No data localisation requirements). No subsequent legislation introducing localisation requirements was found as of the most recent secondary commentary (2023-2024).
revised_comments: Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022) does not impose a data localisation requirement. Part V of the Act (sections 32 and 33) permits cross-border transfer of personal information to other SADC member states under regional data protection standards, and to non-SADC states subject to an assessment that the recipient jurisdiction affords an adequate level of data protection. There is no legal provision mandating that personal, government, financial or other categories of data be stored within Eswatini's borders.
